# The {2,3}-Substrate Cluster — Four-Way Bijection Family

This file states the cluster theorem: the substrate ((ℤ/2)³ \ {0})
admits canonical partition-preserving bijections to four contexts —
Trivium quadratic discriminants, Fano plane points, Steane code basis
qubits, and 𝕋₇ Klein-bottle Möbius strips. All four labelings share
the Hamming-weight (3, 3, 1) partition.

## What this file proves

A single packaged theorem `cluster_bijection_family` asserting that
Test 1 passes for all four pairwise bijections (substrate to each of
Trivium / Fano / Steane / 𝕋₇).

The pairwise component theorems are in the companion files:
  • `TriviumLabeling.lean` — substrate ↔ Trivium discriminants
  • `FanoLabeling.lean`    — substrate ↔ Fano points
  • `SteaneLabeling.lean`  — substrate ↔ Steane qubits
  • `T7Labeling.lean`      — substrate ↔ 𝕋₇ strips

Through composition, any two of the four contexts are also in
canonical partition-preserving bijection. The cluster theorem
packages the full family.

Vanilla Lean 4. No Mathlib. No sorry. No axioms.
rows.licensed: cluster_bijection_family packages the four forward weight-preservation theorems; the bijections are the companion files' inverse theorems, compositions are compiled for Trivium-Fano and Steane-T7, and pairwise preservation by composition is elementary; no sorry or axiom keyword at the pin and no banked print for this kernel.

# Fano Labeling of the Substrate

This file establishes the canonical bijection between the substrate
((ℤ/2)³ \ {0}) and the points of the Fano plane PG(2, 𝔽₂), per
FANO_PLANE_OF_ARITHMETIC.

## The labeling

Each Fano point [x : y : z] over 𝔽₂ has exactly one nonzero
representative (since 𝔽₂ has no nontrivial scalar multiples). The
seven Fano points are:

  • [1 : 0 : 0], [0 : 1 : 0], [0 : 0 : 1] — weight 1
  • [1 : 1 : 0], [1 : 0 : 1], [0 : 1 : 1] — weight 2
  • [1 : 1 : 1]                            — weight 3

The bijection to substrate identifies each Fano point with the
substrate element having matching bit pattern.

## What this file proves

  • Canonical bijection `Substrate.toFano : Substrate → FanoPoint`
  • Inverse `FanoPoint.toSubstrate`
  • Bijection identities (left and right inverse)
  • Hamming weight preserved (Test 1 passes)

Vanilla Lean 4. No Mathlib. No sorry. No axioms.

# Steane Labeling of the Substrate

This file establishes the canonical bijection between the substrate
((ℤ/2)³ \ {0}) and the physical qubits of the Steane code [[7, 1, 3]],
per ARITHMETIC_ORIGIN_STEANE_CODE_v3 and FANO_PLANE_OF_ARITHMETIC.

## The labeling

The Steane code [[7, 1, 3]] is a quantum CSS code built from the
classical [7, 4, 3] Hamming code. The parity-check matrix of the
Hamming code has seven columns, each a nonzero element of (𝔽₂)³.
Each physical qubit of the Steane code corresponds to one column.

The qubits are indexed q1 through q7, with the bijection to substrate
established by matching each qubit to the substrate element whose
bit pattern matches the qubit's column position in the parity-check
matrix.

## Column weight

The Hamming weight of a substrate element equals the column weight in
the parity-check matrix — the number of stabilizer generators that
act nontrivially on the corresponding qubit. This is the
partition-preserving correspondence (Test 1) between substrate and
Steane qubits.

## What this file proves

  • Canonical bijection `Substrate.toSteane : Substrate → SteaneQubit`
  • Inverse `SteaneQubit.toSubstrate`
  • Bijection identities (left and right inverse)
  • Column weight matches Hamming weight (Test 1 passes)

Vanilla Lean 4. No Mathlib. No sorry. No axioms.

# The {2,3}-Substrate

This file formalizes the substrate underlying the {2,3}-cluster:
the nontrivial elements of (ℤ/2)³, with the canonical Hamming-weight
partition (3, 3, 1).

## What's enumerated

`Substrate` — the nontrivial elements of (ℤ/2)³, indexed by their
binary representation:

  • b100, b010, b001 (weight 1)
  • b110, b101, b011 (weight 2)
  • b111             (weight 3)

## Why this substrate matters

Per the corpus, four contexts realize (ℤ/2)³ \ {0} canonically:

  • Trivium quadratic discriminants from generators {2, 3, −1}
    (TRIVIUM_The_Third_Identity_Element §3, FANO_PLANE_OF_ARITHMETIC)
  • Fano plane PG(2, 𝔽₂) points
    (FANO_PLANE_OF_ARITHMETIC, phase2_fano_plane.pdf)
  • Steane code [[7, 1, 3]] basis qubits via Hamming [7, 4, 3]
    coordinate matrix (ARITHMETIC_ORIGIN_STEANE_CODE_v3)
  • 𝕋₇ Klein-bottle topology Möbius strips
    (CORPUS_CATALOGOS §C.3, klein_trivium.pdf)

Each of these realizations is a canonical labeling of the same
underlying substrate. The partition by Hamming weight (3, 3, 1)
lifts to a partition-preserving bijection across the four contexts
— passing Test 1 (structure-preserving bijection) in all six pairwise
directions.

This kernel formalizes the substrate and its partition. Canonical
labelings (one per context) are formalized in companion modules; the
present module is the substrate-level theorem.

## What this file proves

  • Substrate is enumerated as a 7-element type
  • Hamming weight is computable on each element
  • The partition by weight has cardinalities (3, 3, 1)

## Relation to retracted convergent-seven framing

The v0.2 SIDE-meta convergent-seven synthesis claimed a five-way
collapse of equi-cardinal sets including the mechanism classes of
ξ(s). That synthesis was wrong: the mechanism-class set has
partition (2, 3, 2) by formation stage, which does not match
(3, 3, 1) — the §216 obstruction. The substrate-cluster (this
kernel's subject) is the structural family that DOES collapse
canonically. Test 1 passes for the substrate cluster precisely
because partition matches; Test 1 failed for the mechanism classes
precisely because partition does not match. The discipline:
substrate-cluster work is the positive case where the bijection
synthesis was structurally justified; convergent-seven was the
overreach.

Vanilla Lean 4. No Mathlib. No sorry. No axioms.

# 𝕋₇ Labeling of the Substrate

This file establishes the canonical bijection between the substrate
((ℤ/2)³ \ {0}) and the Möbius strips of the Klein-bottle topology
𝕋₇, per klein_trivium.pdf (Seven Möbius Strips on a Fano Frame).

## The labeling

Each Trivium quadratic field K = ℚ(√d) for d ∈ {−1, 2, 3, −2, −3, 6, −6}
carries the glide reflection φ : s ↦ 1 − s̄ on its critical strip. The
quotient is a Möbius strip. The seven strips share the critical line
σ = 1/2 as common boundary.

The strips are labeled by their discriminant d, and the bijection to
substrate uses the same {2, 3, −1} bit-pattern encoding as the Trivium
labeling (TriviumLabeling.lean). The structural distinction: Trivium
discriminants are algebraic objects (quadratic fields); 𝕋₇ strips are
topological objects (Möbius surfaces). The labels coincide; the
underlying mathematical content differs.

## What this file proves

  • Canonical bijection `Substrate.toT7 : Substrate → T7Strip`
  • Inverse `T7Strip.toSubstrate`
  • Bijection identities (left and right inverse)
  • Hamming weight preserved (Test 1 passes)

Vanilla Lean 4. No Mathlib. No sorry. No axioms.

# Trivium Labeling of the Substrate

This file establishes the canonical bijection between the substrate
((ℤ/2)³ \ {0}) and the Trivium quadratic discriminants of
TRIVIUM_The_Third_Identity_Element §3 (Proposition 3.2), with the
Hamming-weight partition (3, 3, 1) preserved.

## The labeling

The Trivium generators are {2, 3, −1}. Each discriminant corresponds
to a subset of these generators, read as a binary triple:

  • (1, 0, 0) ↔ −1     ↔ ℚ(i)
  • (0, 1, 0) ↔  2     ↔ ℚ(√2)
  • (0, 0, 1) ↔  3     ↔ ℚ(√3)
  • (1, 1, 0) ↔ −2     ↔ ℚ(√−2)
  • (1, 0, 1) ↔ −3     ↔ ℚ(√−3)
  • (0, 1, 1) ↔  6     ↔ ℚ(√6)
  • (1, 1, 1) ↔ −6     ↔ ℚ(√−6)

The TriviumDisc type is vendored from SIDE-meta v0.3 with attribution
(federation discipline: cross-kernel content is vendored, not imported
via Lake dependencies).

## What this file proves

  • A canonical bijection `Substrate.toTrivium : Substrate → TriviumDisc`
  • Its inverse `TriviumDisc.toSubstrate`
  • The bijection is a left-inverse and right-inverse pair
  • The bijection preserves Hamming weight (Test 1 passes)

## Test 1 in positive direction

This is the case where the structure-preserving bijection synthesis is
structurally justified: substrate and Trivium discriminants share the
same (3, 3, 1) Hamming-weight partition, and the bijection is canonical.
Contrast with the convergent-seven framing in v0.2 SIDE-meta where the
attempted bijection failed Test 1 because the partition structures
differed.
